codes.evidence_quote: That which we call "compás" and define as division in exact counts of a musical measure must be indestructible and indispensable if flamenco is to maintain its expressive capacity.
codes.target: compás as a criterion of flamenco dance and expressive capacity
codes.rationale: The passage defines compás as an indispensable aesthetic criterion for maintaining flamenco's expressive value.

codes.evidence_quote: The baile becomes a mighty hurricane that overthrows conventions when this man executes it.

codes.evidence_quote: Only geniuses can divide or multiply for themselves these musical phases without losing a note of their reality and with perfect subjugation to the pre-set structure.
codes.target: artists capable of manipulating compás without losing structure
codes.rationale: The passage constructs a hierarchy in which only exceptional artists can legitimately alter musical phases while preserving flamenco structure.

possible_but_not_emitted.reason: The text mentions evolution while remaining faithful to constants, but the claim functions mainly as an aesthetic criterion rather than a tradition/continuity argument.

codes.evidence_quote: Students come from all over the USA and Canada to learn flamenco dance. Some have no prior dance or flamenco experience. Others are dance teachers and advanced dance students.
codes.rationale: The passage frames the workshop as a transnational learning-access site for beginners and advanced students from the USA and Canada.

codes.evidence_quote: Teo defined flamenco terminology; desplante, llamada, escobilla, etc. He explained the development of a flamenco dancer
codes.rationale: Teo is positioned as an authoritative teacher who defines terminology and explains flamenco dancer development.

codes.evidence_quote: Palmas, with the guitar, provide the rhythm. For the student, palmas reinforce compás. Further, there is participation by the jaleadores, signaling feedback and appreciation of the dancer.
codes.target: palmas, compás, and jaleo in workshop learning
codes.rationale: The passage describes embodied and participatory learning of rhythm, compás, and performance feedback.

codes.evidence_quote: He traced the evolution of the dance from around the campfire to the elaborate Las Vegas-type productions found in the modern big city tablaos. According to Teo, there is valid artistic expression to be found in both forms.
codes.target: campfire flamenco and modern big-city tablao productions
codes.rationale: The passage uses Teo's expert framing to contest a simple boundary that would delegitimate staged or commercial forms.

possible_but_not_emitted.reason: Jaleadores and participation are discussed, but the passage primarily treats them as pedagogical performance elements rather than a public/private participatory value contrast.

The text discusses business and Las Vegas-type tablaos, but it explicitly avoids framing commercialization as an authenticity threat.
